title: Fix sub-minute usage rounding drift and reconcile reserved capacity credit merges
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
We are observing repeated invoice-level discrepancies caused by cent-level rounding errors when merging high-frequency (sub-minute) metering pulses into reserved-capacity credit buckets. The export job that materializes invoice lines collapses multi-sample sub-minute usage into single invoice lines using a naive floating-point sum + round-to-cent step. Under concurrent ingestion and retry conditions this produces non-deterministic cent drift and duplicate small-credit lines in Stripe/NetSuite exports.

Impact:
- Affected customers receive invoices with small mismatched line totals (typical magnitude: $0.01-$1.20).
- Finance reconciliations require manual adjustments for mid-cycle reserved-capacity bursts.
- Automated reconciler alerts are firing and backfills create duplicate corrections.

Reproduction steps:
1) Run the hourly aggregator on synthetic events with sub-minute pulses (e.g., 10–30s intervals) targeting reserved capacity plans.
2) Enable ingestion retries (simulate transient DB errors) so pulses are deduplicated later in the pipeline.
3) Execute export job with current merge algorithm (float sum then round).
4) Observe per-invoice line total differences when comparing export run A vs run B; occasional non-idempotent small credit lines manifest.

Hypothesis / Root cause:
- Floating-point accumulation + ad-hoc cent rounding yields different results depending on aggregation order (non-associative).
- Concurrent dedupe/retry windows change the effective merge ordering leading to off-by-one-cent differences.
- The export schema is not enforcing stable, deterministic tie-breaking for subminute buckets and credit merges.

Proposed solution (multiphase):
Phase 1 (safety hotfix):
- Switch export accumulators to integer minor-units (cents) at the earliest bucketing stage. Avoid floating sums entirely.
- Add deterministic sort key for merge ordering: (tenant_id, invoice_period_start, usage_window_microbucket, provider_shard).
- Add a quick compensating reconcile step that collapses duplicate micro-credit lines into a single line with consolidated cents before Stripe/NetSuite line emission.
Phase 2 (longer-term):
- Replace current sub-minute bucketing with explicit microbucket (e.g., 10s) and persist bucketed deltas as epoched ledger entries to make merges idempotent.
- Add export seqnum + checksum signature to each generated invoice export to detect non-idempotent replays.
- Update backfill tool to use deterministic merge semantics and a repair-runner that outputs a signed patch manifest.
Phase 3 (observability + validation):
- Add a reconciliation job that compares exported invoice totals to ledger-anchored totals and emits diffs to Slack/GSI for > $0.50 anomalies.
- Add dashboards: cent-error-distribution, export-idempotency-rate, microbucket-collision-rate.

Acceptance criteria:
- Exported invoice lines are stable and repeatable for identical input sets (idempotency verified via checksum).
- Cent-level discrepancies reduced to zero in synthetic replay tests and < 0.01% in production over 7d window.
- Backfill runs produce no duplicate credit lines and add an audit manifest for each modification.

Rollback plan:
- Revert to old accumulator only if we observe any > $5 regressions within 24 hours. The hotfix is isolated behind a feature-flag (billing.export_integer_accumulator). Reverting flag restores previous aggregation path.

Testing / QA plan:
- Unit tests that assert integer-cent accumulation invariants across permutations of ordering (use randomized property tests).
- Integration test that replays recorded production pulses and asserts checksum stability across two independent export runs.
- Canary on a single low-volume org for 48 hours before broad rollout.

Monitoring / Runbook:
- New alert: export-cent-diff-rate > 0.1% triggers on-call.
- Dashboard link: billing-exports/cent-stability (will be created in Console).
- Runbook steps: 1) toggle feature flag, 2) run repair manifest, 3) open finance reconciliation ticket with manifest attached.

Notes / Links:
- Design doc (internal): drive.redwood/billing/cent-rounding-fix (pending upload).
- PR for integer accumulator: github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4021 (WIP).
- Related tickets: ENG-902001 (hourly window skew), ENG-827465 (concurrent export leader election).
